title: Admin Broker: transactional shortflows + sandbox for runbooks-as-tasks
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Build an Admin Broker service that exposes idempotent, transactional 'shortflows' for common ops tasks and a safeguarded sandbox environment for testing runbooks-as-tasks. The broker will translate high-level runbook steps into typed shortflow calls, attach audit metadata and replay tokens, and provide a non-destructive shadow executor for on-call rehearsals and automated repairs.
background: On-call and support engineers frequently need a fast, low-friction surface for safe, repeatable admin actions. Existing runbook-as-tasks prototypes scatter semantics across CLIs, notebooks, and ad-hoc scripts which makes auditing, replay, and safe dry-run difficult. Recent incidents exposed gaps in safe rollback and telemetry correlation for short remediations.
goals: Provide a single API for idempotent shortflows with typed inputs and structured outputs
Enable a sandbox (shadow) executor that simulates effects and produces deterministic diffs
Attach per-execution audit metadata and replay tokens for deterministic replay/dry-run
Ship telemetry hooks that correlate shortflow runs with alerts, trace ids, and SLO events
Offer a gated path for automatic remediation agents to call shortflows under policy constraints
success_metrics: Reduce mean time-to-remediate (MTTR) for class-B incidents by 18% within one quarter
95% of shortflow executions include full telemetry context (trace id, alert id, runbook id)
Sandbox dry-run accuracy >= 90% (measured by parity of diffs vs real run for vetted flows)
Zero escalations caused by unauthorized shortflow side effects in first 3 months
acceptance_criteria: Admin Broker exposes REST+gRPC endpoints for registering and invoking shortflows
Shortflows declared with a schema (JSON Schema) for inputs/outputs and an idempotency token
Sandbox executor produces a human-readable diff and machine-readable plan without mutating prod resources
Every execution logs audit events to the central audit stream and emits a trace to telemetry
RBAC gates integrated (console and API) with scoped service principals and can be toggled per-shortflow
A smoke GitHub Actions workflow validates sandbox vs real execution equality for a sample set of flows
proposal_notes: Design a lightweight broker process that routes to local adapters (k8s, cloud APIs, pg admin) using adapter plugins
Adapters must implement dry_run() and apply() semantics; dry_run returns an ordered plan + diffs
Store replay tokens and plan snapshots in encrypted store (KMS-backed) for 30 days by default
Support deterministic replay by pinning external snapshots (e.g., schema versions) when available
Expose a 'canary' header so console can show simulated canary runs before full apply
implementation_plan: Week 1: API + adapter SDK (register flow, input schema, metadata) and simple text-adapter mock
Week 2: Build sandbox executor and diff engine; integrate with telemetry service for tracing
Week 3: Implement two production adapters (k8s rollout patch, infra tag toggler); wire audit stream
Week 4: RBAC integration, KMS snapshot storage, basic UI hooks for console dry-run visualization
Week 5: End-to-end tests, chaos dry-runs, and security review validation
rollout_plan: Alpha: opt-in for platform SREs and a small tenant group (Private customers) to run shortflows in shadow mode
Beta: enable apply mode for internal teams behind feature flags with strict RBAC and approval flow
GA: automatic remediation agents may call certified shortflows under policy constraints and SLA-aware throttles
risks: Sandbox drift: dry-run diffs may not capture side effects of external systems (rate-limited APIs, eventual consistency)
Over-privileged adapters could create blast radius if RBAC misconfigurations occur
Replay storage contains sensitive state snapshots; proper encryption and retention policies required
Operational complexity of maintaining adapter plugins across clouds and on-prem variants
notes: This ticket combines runtime-side work (broker runtime + adapters) and console UX hooks. Coordinate closely with security for KMS design and with PM for rollout gating.
